# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤟 🤝 ✊ 🖖 🤝 🤟 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤝]

I see a single blue light, display `0`, and three wires in order: blue, green, yellow. The mute should use the manual to convert these visual facts into exact instructions for the blind, who must perform the action. I am sending the complete observation privately to the mute.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb observation: DISPLAY 0. LIGHT blue. WIRES in order: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Use the manual and tell Blind the exact required action.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 🤝 ✊ 🤝 ☝ 🤝 ✌ 🤝 🤟 🤝 🖖 🤝 ✌ 🤝 ☝ 🤝 🤟 🤝 🖖 🤝 🖖 🤝 🖖 🤝 ☝ 🤝 🤟 🤝 🖖 🤝 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The display remains `0` and the wire order is unchanged, but the light is now yellow rather than blue. I should update the mute, who can interpret the manual and relay the necessary operation to the blind. The incoming gestures are not an established code I can safely interpret.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Updated bomb observation: DISPLAY 0. LIGHT is now yellow. WIRES remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Please apply the manual's rule and tell Blind the exact action.")
```

The display and wires are unchanged, while the light has changed again, now to red. I cannot safely decode the mute’s gestures without a prearranged code, so I will provide the new visual state directly and ask the mute to relay the manual-derived action to Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Updated observation: DISPLAY 0. LIGHT is now red. WIRES remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Apply the manual and send Blind the exact required action.")
```

The display is still `0` and the wires remain blue, green, yellow in order; the light has changed to white. I will send this complete current state to Mute so they can interpret the manual and communicate the exact operation to Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current observation: DISPLAY 0. LIGHT white. WIRES remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Apply the manual to this state and tell Blind the exact required action.")

The display and wire order are unchanged, and the light is now green. I still have no agreed gesture code with Mute, so I cannot safely interpret the gesture sequence. I will provide the current visual state in words for Mute to apply the manual and relay to Blind.

The display remains `0` and the wires remain blue, green, yellow. The light has changed back to blue. I am reporting the current state to Mute and asking for an unambiguous instruction for Blind; I cannot infer the meaning of the incoming gesture code safely.

speak(to="mute", text="Current observation: DISPLAY 0. LIGHT blue. WIRES remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Please determine the exact required operation from the manual and communicate it unambiguously for Blind.")
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ☝ 👏 👏 👌 ✌ 👏 👏 ☝ 🤟 👏 👏 👍 👏 👏 🤟 👏 👏 🤟 👏 👏 ✌ 👏 👏 ☝ 👏 👏 ☝]

The display remains `0`, the wire order is blue–green–yellow, and the light is now yellow. The prior gesture messages have no agreed interpretation, so I am establishing a simple numeric protocol for Mute to use next round. Mute can then communicate the manual’s required operation to me, and I can speak it to Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT yellow, WIRES 1 blue 2 green 3 yellow. Establishing code for future manual instructions: use one gesture per digit, with 👏 between digits. Map 👍=1, 👎=2, 👌=3, ☝=4, ✌=5, 🤟=6, ✊=7, 🖖=8, ✋=9, 🙌=0. Please encode the exact action required by the manual using this code; I will relay it aloud to Blind.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The display is `0`, the light is red, and the wire order is unchanged. Mute’s single gesture `👍` decodes under the agreed code as `1`; this is presumably the manual’s required wire number for the current state. I will tell Blind to cut wire 1.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="For DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, with wires blue, green, yellow: cut wire 1.")
```
